bullets.title: Treasury's $10B Duration Swap: Mini-Twist With Macro Risk — Jackson Hole Key
bullets.body: Treasury announced a ~$10B duration swap running Sept 9–Nov 4, roughly 1/60th the size of the Fed's 2011 Operation Twist, which pulled 30-year yields ~150bps. JPM is skeptical the buyback resolves the funding problem — it merely reallocates deficit burden to the front end without fiscal consolidation. If the Fed steps in to buy bill issuance funding long-end duration retirement, the operation escalates to a joint Fed-Treasury intervention; multiple desks see Jackson Hole (Aug 27-29, Warsh speaking Aug 28) as the venue where policy direction gets signaled.

bullets.title: August Philly Fed Surges to 47.4% (Strongest Since Spring 2021); Jobless Claims 206K
bullets.body: The August Philadelphia Manufacturing Index hit 47.4%, up 6 points MoM and the strongest reading since spring 2021; ISM-adjusted equivalent at 57.5%. Initial jobless claims printed 206K, beating 210K consensus and down 6K WoW. Capital expenditure plans are at their highest since the 1970s, while price expectations remain elevated — pointing to sticky inflation even as current price metrics decelerate.

bullets.title: August Inflation Nowcast at +3.48% Y/Y (+12bps Sequential Acceleration); Rate Hike Risk Re-emerges
bullets.body: The August inflation nowcast shows headline CPI at +3.48% Y/Y, a +12bps sequential acceleration from July. Multiple desks note that if Bessent's buyback effort succeeds in suppressing long-end yields in a 5.7% nominal GDP environment, it may necessitate direct Fed rate hikes to manage inflation — FOMC minutes have already confirmed rate cuts are fully off the table.

bullets.title: Tech Momentum Unwind: High-Beta Basket -7.3%, Pure Momentum -5% in Two Days
bullets.body: A sharp momentum/growth unwind accelerated over two sessions — the High Beta Momentum basket fell 7.3% on the day and Tech Momentum is down ~18% over two days, driven by quant/systematic de-risking and hedge fund liquidation. The S&P masked the damage, closing +21bps, while QQQ fell 20bps and Nasdaq 100 futures extended their decline to -0.5%. Semis and Infrastructure Software were the hardest hit; Mag7 cohorts are showing differentiated rather than monolithic price action.

bullets.title: Healthcare Short Squeeze Erupts: Most-Shorted Basket +6.4% on Day, +31.5% in 3 Months
bullets.body: The consensus hedge fund healthcare short basket surged 6.4% in a single session, extending a 31.5% gain over three months. Healthcare (XLV) is up 10.7% QTD vs. Utilities (XLU) down 2.9% and Tech (XLK) down 1.1%, representing one of the sharpest sector rotations in recent history. Hedgeye flagged this as one of the best days in market history for the Healthcare Long vs. Tech Short pair trade.

bullets.title: Dollar Weakness Accelerating: USD -1% Over Two Days, -2.5% QTD; Gold +4%, Bitcoin to $71K
bullets.body: The USD Index fell ~1% over two days and is down 2.5% quarter-to-date, accelerating global dollar-liquidity measures. Gold rose nearly 4% on the dollar move with miners posting high-single to low-double-digit gains; GDX is up 40% since its mid-July low. Bitcoin crossed $71K and broke above its 200-day moving average for the first time since the recent selloff, triggering a record $2.73B in crypto short liquidations.

bullets.title: US National Debt Crosses $40 Trillion; Interest Expense $3.8B/Day, Exceeding Medicare and Defense
bullets.body: US national debt surpassed $40 trillion for the first time as borrowing accelerates at a historic pace. The government now spends $3.8B/day on debt interest, outpacing Medicare ($3.1B/day) and Defense ($2.5B/day), with investor concerns about fiscal sustainability growing despite Trump administration pledges to control spending.

bullets.title: Energy: Oil at One-Month Highs; Brent +8% on Week; Diesel Crack at Record $104/Barrel
bullets.body: Brent crude hit a one-month high, rising +8% on the week on Iran geopolitical pressures and Strait of Hormuz disruption concerns — Iran has reportedly lost significant control of the strait per CNN. European gas prices surged to €65/MWh (highest since March), EU storage sits at 62% capacity. US gasoline rose to $4.1/gallon while diesel crack spreads hit a record $104/barrel with US diesel reserves at 23-year lows, supporting a refining "golden age" thesis.

bullets.title: AI Capex Described as "Largest Capex-Driven GDP Boost in History" (Bloomberg)
bullets.body: Bloomberg and multiple sell-side desks characterize AI infrastructure investment as delivering the largest capex-driven GDP boost in history, with data centers, semiconductors, cloud infrastructure, and energy capacity seeing unprecedented capital deployment. Top 1% AI adopters are increasing spend 50% and top 10% up 25% as costs fall, indicating elastic demand among advanced users. 22V notes Anthropic IPO (early October) and CME compute futures launch (Oct 5) as near-term AI infrastructure catalysts.

bullets.title: US-China AI Race Framing Shifts to Full-Stack Control; Two Distinct Ecosystems Emerging
bullets.body: DA Davidson panel described the AI race as shifting from competition over the smartest models to a fight for full-stack control across chips, cloud, power, data, developers, and regulatory frameworks. China is advancing a self-reliant AI ecosystem around Huawei, Alibaba, Tencent, and DeepSeek with lower-cost models and alternative compute, while export controls, data sovereignty, and regulatory divergence are creating two distinct AI ecosystems that enterprises must navigate.

bullets.title: Upcoming Macro Catalysts: NVDA Earnings Aug 26, Jackson Hole Aug 27-29, PCE Aug 26
bullets.body: JPM's macro calendar flags NVDA earnings on Aug 26 as a major near-term catalyst; Hedgeye expects NVDA to beat with better guidance, with the magnitude of order growth and incremental AI infrastructure demand being the key variables. Jackson Hole symposium runs Aug 27-29 with Fed Chair Warsh speaking Aug 28 morning, followed by PCE data also on Aug 26. AVGO earnings follow on Sept 2.

bullets.title: Walmart Q2: EPS Beat on Tariff Refunds, but US Comps Miss at +2.6% vs. +3.7% Est.; Stock -7%
bullets.body: WMT reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.81 (+19% YoY), well above guidance of $0.72-$0.74, boosted by ~$3B in tariff refunds. However, US comps ex-gas came in at +2.6% vs. consensus +3.5-3.7%, partly due to a 125bps headwind from Maximum Fair Pricing legislation on health/wellness. Q3 EPS guidance of $0.62-$0.64 was below consensus of $0.67-$0.68, sending the stock down ~7% premarket and pressuring retail sympathy names.

bullets.title: Active Funds Rotated Out of Momentum/Semis in 2Q; Hyperscaler Holdings Quietly Increased
bullets.body: Quant data shows active funds slashed momentum and growth exposure — particularly semiconductors and tech hardware — following the late-June momentum crash, shifting into value and risk-on cyclicals. However, hyperscaler median share holdings actually increased 2.7% despite AI ROI concerns, suggesting institutional conviction in mega-cap cloud remains intact even as the broader AI trade was trimmed.

bullets.title: Hedgeye Model Forecasting Shift From Monthly Quad 3 to Monthly Quad 1 Next Month
bullets.body: Hedgeye's macro model is forecasting a transition from Monthly Quad 3 to Monthly Quad 1 next month, implying a shift toward a growth-accelerating, inflation-decelerating macro regime. This supports their current positioning: long Healthcare (XLV), long Energy, short USD, long Gold, with S&P immediate-term risk range at 7652-7815 and 10-year yield range 4.61-4.74%.

bullets.title: German 5-Year Yield Hits 3% for First Time Since 2008; European Gas €65/MWh
bullets.body: German 5-year yields touched 3% for the first time since 2008, reflecting tighter European monetary conditions and rising inflation expectations. European gas simultaneously hit €65/MWh, the highest since March, adding to energy-driven cost pressures across the continent even as EU Commission says storage at 62% presents no immediate supply emergency.

bullets.title: Copper Supply Squeeze: Biggest Weekly LME Warehouse Inflows Since 2020
bullets.body: A copper supply squeeze is drawing the biggest weekly flow into LME sheds since 2020, signaling acute physical market tightness. This comes alongside Taiwan suppliers expanding copper-clad laminate (CCL) capacity for AI/data center PCB demand, though capacity additions are reportedly running behind schedule.

bullets.title: Diesel Crack Spread at Record $104/Barrel; Refining "Golden Age" Thesis Gaining Traction
bullets.body: Diesel crack spreads hit a record $104/barrel as US diesel reserves sit at 23-year lows and European stockpiles near 2022 crisis levels, with Russia's refining capacity approximately one-third offline due to war disruption. Morgan Stanley's energy desk is bullish on a multi-year "golden age" for refining with global fuel inventories at 2022 lows, a 10-12 year build cycle for new capacity, and GRMs expected to settle 30% above prior mid-cycle.

bullets.title: M&A Volumes Down 5% Y/Y in 3Q26 QTD; Equity Issuance +78% Led by Record APAC
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Deal Dashboard shows announced M&A volume down 5% Y/Y in 3Q26 QTD (vs. flat in prior quarter), with North America particularly weak at -14% Y/Y while Europe leads at +23% Y/Y. Equity issuance is the bright spot at +78% Y/Y driven by record APAC volume. DCM is weak with HY bonds and leveraged loans both down ~41-42% Y/Y; deal activity is expected to be back-end weighted toward September.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz Risk Elevated; Iran Losing Control, Gulf of Aden Hijacking Reported
bullets.body: Iran has reportedly lost significant control of the Strait of Hormuz per CNN, with outbound energy tanker transits down to 4/day from 6/day. A tanker was hijacked in the Gulf of Aden and redirected to Somalia. Middle East crude exports averaged 6.0 mmbbl/d last week, down -2.2 mmbbl/d WoW, with Qatar mediating US-Iran discussions described by the White House as stalled weeks ago.

bullets.title: 2% US Growth Speed Limit May Constrain Yield Suppression Efforts — Macro Strategist
bullets.body: MacDonell (via JATCapital forward) argues US financial markets are functioning normally, credit channels are open, and there is no liquidity trap — making Treasury/Fed yield manipulation efforts "pointless" rather than bad. Forcing long-end yields lower would breach the ~2% structural growth speed limit imposed by collapsed population growth and inflation constraints, requiring offsetting Fed tightening. The strategist notes 2% growth is not problematic for equities if profit margins remain structurally wide.
